_about: The Japan Trip Kit's nine route SPINES (2026-09-12; v2 2026-09-13 — PLAN-spines.md, "decisions belong to cities and legs").
A spine is an ordered list of major CITIES, and every decision hangs off a city or off the leg between two cities, so a
chosen place can only land where it belongs — nothing can be put before Kyoto, and two ryokan on different legs are two
separate yes/no answers rather than one either/or.
`cities` is the spine, in trip order: either a loc key string (a fixed city) or a CITY switch
{kind:"city", key, question, default, options[{label, desc, cities[], …}]} — the start (Tokyo first or straight into the
region), the Kansai choice (always symmetric: Kyoto | Osaka | Kyoto and Osaka), the direction, the end city. A CITY option
may carry `in`/`out` (the airport it implies), `line` (the one-liner printed when it is taken — the blurb follows the route,
so a start that drops Tokyo does not still describe one), `reverse: true` (the middle of the route runs the other way; a
leading or trailing Tokyo stays put) and the guards below.
`attach` are the ATTACHMENTS: a yes/no night that belongs to one city — {key, city[], kind: inn|stop, at: split|after|before,
question, desc, no, stops[], default, on_at?}. `city` is a list: the first of those cities present on the assembly owns it
(so Nara attaches after Kyoto, or between Kyoto and Osaka, and never before Kyoto). `at` says how it sits: `split` puts the
city, the attachment, then the city again (Nikkō out and back splits the Tokyo stay), `after` and `before` put it on one side.
`legs` are the LEG SLOTS: {key, from[], to[], slots[{key, kind, question, desc, no, stops[], default, on_at?}]}. A leg is
offered when one of its `from` cities and one of its `to` cities are consecutive on the assembly, either way round; its slots
are the ryokan towns and the STOP towns that sit on that leg, each a yes/no, inserted in the order they are declared. Two
slots on two different legs are two answers: Yudanaka before Kanazawa AND Kaga after it, on one trip.
`end` is the END decision, unchanged: how the trip finishes — fly from the last city, one more ryokan night, or back through
Tokyo — with `stops[]`, `place: after|before <loc>` and `out` as before.
Decision keys are what `--set` takes: `start`, `kansai`, `end` for the switches, `<city>.<name>` for an attachment
(`--set tokyo.nikko=yes`), `<leg>.<name>` for a leg slot (`--set tokyo-kanazawa.yudanaka=yes`). Yes/no answers take `yes`/`no`
or the option number; a switch takes its label or number. The engine derives one flat decision list from all of this and
prints it grouped in trip order — a city, its attachment, the leg's slots, the next city — and a decision whose only real
option is withheld here is never shown.
Guards, on any option: `requires` / `not_with` (loc keys that must be, or must not be, on the route — `tokyo@first` means
Tokyo must open the trip), `or_in` (arrival airport codes that waive `requires`: a booked flight into the region settles a
guard about landing straight at a ryokan), `why_not` (the sentence the tool and the explorer print when it is withheld). An
attachment whose city is not on the route, and a slot whose leg is not on the route, are withheld the same way. A `--in`
ticket also PICKS the START option that declares that same `in`, unless `--set start=` says otherwise.
`name` is the spine's short name, `blurb` the longer line it used to be called by, `for` the one line that says who it is for
(the menu's For column), `rank` the menu order for a first visit and a repeat one (1 is offered first), `assumes: "repeat"`
that the For line takes a traveller who has already done Tokyo and Kyoto. `band` is the night range the spine is meant for
(four lower when the START option drops Tokyo); `draws` are Stage 1's draws it answers (food temples nature onsen craft city
pop art snow coast). `default` is the option taken when nothing is chosen; `on_at: N` makes a yes/no default to yes at a
requested total of N nights or more.
Nights are never part of a decision: each place starts at its places.json ideal low (a repeated city splits 3/2 for Tokyo,
2/1 otherwise) and `spine --nights loc=N` or `--total N` moves them inside the ranges. Nothing here carries a travel time.
The route engine (builder/route.js `spines`, `spine`, `compare`) assembles, prices and checks every assembly through
buildPlan; build-kit.js prints the menu and the nine spines into the kit and emits guides/route-explorer.html from this file
and LEGS; kit-verify.js prices every spine × every option of every decision and fails on any assembly that is not clean.
